name: @pipeworx/mcp-twitch

tools.name: top_games
tools.description: Get the top games currently being streamed on Twitch, ranked by number of viewers. Returns game id, name, and box art. Example: top_games({ first: 20 })

first.description: Number of games to return (default 20, max 100)

_apiKey.description: Optional — your own Twitch credentials as CLIENT_ID:CLIENT_SECRET for higher limits; omit to use the shared Pipeworx key.

tools.name: get_streams
tools.description: Get live Twitch streams, optionally filtered by game name and/or language. Returns streamer name, title, current viewer count, and thumbnail for each live stream. Omit `game` for the overall top live streams across Twitch. Example: get_streams({ game: "Just Chatting", first: 20, language: "en" })

game.description: Game NAME to filter by (e.g. "Fortnite", "Just Chatting"). Resolved to a game id automatically.

first.description: Number of streams to return (default 20, max 100)

language.description: Optional ISO-639-1 language code to filter by, e.g. "en", "es", "ja".

_apiKey.description: Optional — your own Twitch credentials as CLIENT_ID:CLIENT_SECRET for higher limits; omit to use the shared Pipeworx key.

tools.name: search_channels
tools.description: Search Twitch channels/streamers by name or keyword. Returns matching channels with display name, the game they stream, whether they are live now, title, and thumbnail. Example: search_channels({ query: "ninja", live_only: true })

query.description: Search query — channel/streamer name or keyword, e.g. "ninja", "valorant".

first.description: Number of channels to return (default 20, max 100)

live_only.description: If true, only return channels that are currently live.

_apiKey.description: Optional — your own Twitch credentials as CLIENT_ID:CLIENT_SECRET for higher limits; omit to use the shared Pipeworx key.

tools.name: get_user
tools.description: Look up a Twitch user/channel by login (username). Returns profile info: id, display name, description, view count, broadcaster type, account creation date, and profile image. Example: get_user({ login: "ninja" })

_apiKey.description: Optional — your own Twitch credentials as CLIENT_ID:CLIENT_SECRET for higher limits; omit to use the shared Pipeworx key.

instructions: @pipeworx/mcp-twitch forwards to the Pipeworx gateway and lists only the twitch pack's tools. Set PIPEWORX_META_TOOLS=1 to also list ask_pipeworx and the other gateway-wide tools.
